name: Shrimp Fettuccine Alfredo
description:
Shrimp fettuccine alfredo is one of the best tasting and low effort dishes.
The recipe i give below yields an alfredo sauce that is a bit on the thicker side.
If you want a thinner sauce, adding a touch or two more milk will thin out...

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.originalText: 1/3 cup milk (more milk for thinner sauce)

ingredients.name: Pasta noodles of choice
ingredients.originalText: Pasta noodles of choice (e.g. approximately 9oz of fettuccine noodles)

instructions.text: Read the entire method first and measure the following ingredients before turning on the heat: 1 8oz cream cheese; 1lb uncoocked peeled shrimp; 1/3 cup milk (more milk for thinner sauce); 3/4 cup grated parmesan cheese; 2 tblsp butter; 1 tsp garlic powder; Pasta noodles of choice (e.g. approximately 9oz of fettuccine noodles). Keep ingredients marked optional separate until their step.

Prepare these ingredients before cooking: Shrimp: uncoocked peeled; Parmesan cheese: grated. Wash produce under running water before cutting. Use a cutting board and a sharp knife; keep raw meat and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
Grate your Parmesan Cheese
Peel your shrimp
The dish has two main parts–the Pasta and the Alfredo Sauce.
In order that you can have both finish about the same time, I have given estimates on the individual cook times.
In a medium saucepan, bring 4 cups of water to a rapid boil.
Turn down to medium heat (Simmering). A simmer means small, gentle bubbles; lower the burner if it boils vigorously.
Add your pasta noodles.
In a large frying pan, add butter, garlic powder, and shrimp.
On medium heat, sauté ingredients until shrimp are cooked. Stir frequently so the ingredients soften evenly without sticking or burning; reduce the heat if they darken too quickly.
Then add the cream cheese broken into chunks.
Stir until creamy.
Once cream cheese is to sauce consistency, add milk.
Stir until light simmer. A simmer means small, gentle bubbles; lower the burner if it boils vigorously.
Add parmesan cheese and continue stirring.
Stir until cheese is mixed.
Remove from heat.
Strain cooked pasta noodles. Use the package cooking-time range, stir to separate the pasta, and taste a cooled piece near the end; it should be tender without a hard center.

Before serving, check uncooked fish or shrimp with a food thermometer: it must reach 145°F (63°C). Fish should separate easily into flakes; shrimp should be opaque and firm. Continue cooking and recheck if needed.
Serve the strained noodles on a plate and top with alfredo sauce.

Turn off any burners or oven when cooking is finished. Follow the cooling or resting instruction above before cutting or serving. Serve the finished dish as directed; allow hot portions to cool enough to eat.

source.author: Sergey Bilovytskyy
